doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Who he would see, Coltrane, and Kenny Garrett today
summary: He would go back to see Cannonball and Hendrix; talks about Coltrane's phases and favorite albums.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: If you could — well you had the experience — I was thinking if you could go back in time and see or hear somebody, where would you go.

I would have loved to have seen Cannonball. Because a lot of those live shows, you just wish you were there, you know. Like you hear the crowd and you say yeah, I wish I was there watching that. And Jimi Hendrix. Yeah, you’d like to have been a part of that crowd. Yeah. I would say.
What period of John Coltrane do you especially like?

Yeah. I mean I like his early bebop stages, and that’s the part about him — I like that he transitioned through so many different phases. And I know a lot of people like in the end, you know, he kind of went to outer space, you know, and it’s kind of how he went out. He had like played through every phase in the music and he just took off. I mean I was — just yesterday I was listening to Trane and Bags, you know, with Milt Hinton and the vibe record.

Oh my God, man. The way he could play over a blues. And it’s a lot of notes. Some people say he’s like too notey or whatever, but if you can really catch some of that, it’s like every note is right. It’s perfect. And I do like some of the really hot stuff too, I have to say. Like the album “Transitions” is one of my favorites. “Meditations” is another one. But there’s a lot to listen to with him.
And who would you spend money on these days who is playing now?
Who is playing now. Wow, see I haven’t, that’s a hard one.
It would be hard for me too.
Yes. Yeah. If he came to town I’d go see him. Yeah, definitely, yeah.
